profile.reasoning: Amir Kowalski is a PhD candidate in Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University, specializing in adversarial machine learning for cybersecurity applications. profile.positioning: Amir Kowalski is a PhD candidate at Carnegie Mellon University developing novel defenses against adversarial attacks on machine learning models, with a focus on applications in cybersecurity. His research blends techniques from formal verification and deep learning to enhance the robustness and reliability of AI systems. Recently, Amir presented his work on certified defenses at NeurIPS, demonstrating significant improvements in model resilience. He’s passionate about bridging the gap between academic research and real-world applications, and believes trustworthy AI is critical for a secure future. Amir is actively seeking collaborations and mentorship to translate his research into impactful solutions and explore entrepreneurial opportunities in the AI security space.
